title: A runbook deploys kb_http.py behind an authenticating TLS proxy
goal: kb/_self/hosting.md opens with which path to pick (direct kb_http.py, or a host MCP server embedding kb_mcp.py per kb/_self/embedding.md) and is the runbook for the direct path: a VM with a systemd unit and a reverse proxy that terminates TLS and checks an API-key header (proof of concept) or an Entra token (production), and Azure Container Apps or App Service with built-in authentication; it covers KB_INDEX, a timer that moves the clone to the newest census tag and restarts, one instance per audience because root is a filter and not access control, the network path Copilot Studio needs, and connecting from the MCP onboarding wizard or a custom connector; no secret is in the repository

gates.question: Which hosting does the runbook lead with for the direct kb_http.py path?
options: Azure Container Apps or App Service with built-in authentication (Entra)
A VM with systemd and a reverse proxy (Caddy or nginx)
gates.recommendation: Azure Container Apps or App Service with built-in authentication: no proxy or certificates to run, and Entra tokens validated by the platform; the VM section follows as the proof-of-concept path
gates.answer: Both as equals: two parallel runbook sections (Azure Container Apps or App Service with built-in authentication; a VM with systemd and a reverse proxy), no default
